subject: Geo fallback commitments and test evidence package
messages:
From: Danielle Holt <danielle.holt@lakeshore.com>
To: vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com
Cc: lakeshore-it-security@lakeshore.com, procurement@lakeshore.com
Date: Mon, 16 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Follow-up: failover commitments & evidence for RFP - Lakeshore Financial

Vivek,

Thanks for the initial questionnaire earlier this month. Lakeshore's procurement and security teams reviewed Redwood's answers and have two open asks before we can move to procurement sign-off:

1) A concise mapping of worst-case RTO/RPO per failure mode (region outage, AZ-level network partition, control-plane disruption). Please show the measurable SLA commitments Redwood will accept (e.g., RTO 00:15:00 for X).

2) Test evidence for the most recent multi-region failover rehearsal: runbook used, play-by-play timeline, and post-mortem (including any data-loss evaluation). We need artifacts we can attach to our risk review.

Can you send a single packet that contains a short narrative, the SLA numbers, and the test artifacts (or a link to them)? We prefer a single archive and a proposed rehearsal date for joint observation.

Thanks — we are targeting a decision by month-end if this packet meets our compliance needs.

—Danielle Holt
Head of IT Security, Lakeshore Financial
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
To: Danielle Holt <danielle.holt@lakeshore.com>
Cc: lakeshore-it-security@lakeshore.com, procurement@lakeshore.com, jonas.weber@redwood.com, monica.patel@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 16 Nov 2026 11:02:15 -0800
Subject: Re: Follow-up: failover commitments & evidence for RFP - Lakeshore Financial

Danielle — thanks for the clear asks. Attached is a consolidated evidence bundle and a short narrative. Summary below with the concrete commitments so procurement/security have a single place to review: 

High-level commitments (hosted Redwood production):
- Failure mode: single-AZ outage (application node loss) — Recovery approach: automated instance replacement + KV cache warm-up
  - Commitment (typical): RTO <= 5 minutes for request-serving path; RPO: near-zero for streaming/state (KV cache best-effort warm-up), durable storage consistency within seconds for writes to object-store.
- Failure mode: region-level outage (complete regional eviction) — Recovery approach: DNS-based routing to secondary region + active read replicas + automatic model variant fallback
  - Commitment: RTO <= 15 minutes to return to full-service at equivalent capacity for standard traffic mix; RPO <= 60 seconds for metadata and control-plane records (we persist critical metadata to cross-region replicated storage).
- Failure mode: control-plane disruption (console/API degraded) — Recovery approach: API tier fallbacks routed to dedicated control-plane endpoints + customer-monitored webhook fallbacks
  - Commitment: RTO <= 30 minutes for full control-plane recovery; customer-facing inference endpoints continue on data-plane fallbacks where possible. RPO: administrative metadata may require replay (typical window <= 5 minutes).

Operational notes (short):
- Architecture: active-active routing for inference pod placement with smart routing; durable backing stores use cross-region replication and versioned object buckets; prefix/KV caches are populated via write-through replication during normal ops to minimize drift.
- Model/state sync: KV caches are treated as cache-first; critical state survives in replicated durable store. We employ strict sequence numbers for write order and provide a compact recovery log in the evidence bundle.
- Failover testing: we run quarterly rehearsals plus targeted rehearsals tied to major releases. We keep immutable test artifacts in customer evidence packages.

Attached artifacts (bundle): Redwood_GeoFailover_Runbook_v1.2.pdf (runbook excerpt), DR_Test_Report_20261030.zip (timeline, logs, test harness outputs), rehearsal-schedule-20261120.ics (proposed joint observation window).

Next steps: please confirm whether Lakeshore will observe the rehearsal on 2026-11-20 10:00-12:00 PT (we can shift +/- 48 hours). If that works, Jonas will coordinate a live readout and Monica will provide the test artifacts and a short walkthrough.

If you want us to accept a written SLA appendix for the RFP, indicate which sections of your legal template to sign and we'll route for approvals (we typically accept operational commitments and point to exception language for absolute disaster recovery guarantees).

Regards,

Vivek Kulkarni
VP Product — Redwood Inference
Attachments: Redwood_GeoFailover_Runbook_v1.2.pdf; DR_Test_Report_20261030.zip; rehearsal-schedule-20261120.ics

Looping in Monica and Priyom to confirm artifacts and the rehearsal plan. Monica — I attached the runbook excerpt and full test report in Vivek's packet, but can you also surface the compact recovery log CSV and the recovered-kv-checklist for Lakeshore's review? Priyom — please prepare a 10-minute demonstrator showing automatic routing cutover to secondary region and the DNS health-check timeline (we'll capture video).

Danielle — we can provide a short recorded session of the rehearsal if you prefer not to join live; the live session is preferable for Q&A. We will also include a signed checklist that maps each commitment above to the specific runbook step and observed timestamps from the last rehearsal.

Action items and owners:

Vivek, Jonas — thank you for the quick, comprehensive packet. The numerical commitments and the runbook excerpt look good to our reviewers. A few minor asks before we attach the evidence to the RFP: 

- Please add a one-line statement in the runbook that certifies the timestamps are synchronized to an NTP source and indicate the time source used during the 2026-10-30 rehearsal.
- Could we move the rehearsal window three hours later (2026-11-20 13:00-15:00 PT) to align with our ops team?

If you add the NTP sentence and shift the rehearsal time, procurement will proceed to draft the PO and we will circulate a short technical acceptance to sign. If you prefer, we can watch the recorded rehearsal and still proceed — but the live window is preferred.

Danielle Holt
Head of IT Security, Lakeshore Financial
